risk_reasons: The refactor moves whole-query tenant ownership proofing used before returning draft state or enqueueing generation.
The refactor consolidates PHI screening and review-exception creation on the review-ingestion compliance path.
The refactor centralizes response-version allocation and in-flight outbox detection used by public posting and generation workflows.
goal: Preserve every owner-visible Reply and Review import behavior while issue 765 gives each repeated concurrency, tenancy, polling, compliance, versioning, consent-proof, and cache rule one authoritative owner.
non_goals: Changing any HTTP status, response body, polling completion rule, cache TTL, or owner-facing copy.
Unifying businesses row-lock preambles, Zernio pagination loops, banner and row pollers, account and cookie tenancy, or per-surface completed-branch semantics.
Changing approval, moderation, auto-posting, import-consent, or external-reply-import policy.
Adding a migration, dependency, feature flag, deployment action, or remote operation.
Restoring the deleted KPI service merely to retain the architecture report's former four-call-site cache count.
user_visible_behavior: Owners receive the same edit, regenerate, poll, publish, retry, restore, validation, conflict, and error outcomes as before.
Cross-account and cross-location review or draft probes remain rejected without leaking draft text, status, or moderation heldness.
Reviews likely to contain PHI continue to open the same deduplicated operator exception and skip the same ingestion work.
Import offers and initial imports continue to require the same activation, active-connection, account, archive, and completed-initial-run predicates.
Dashboard location and aggregate payloads retain their 45-second fail-open Redis cache behavior.
Past-replies draft-status responses explicitly carry the existing no-store/private cache policy.
invariants: Issue 765 and docs/reviews/PATHFINDER-2026-08-10/03-unified-proposal.md P4's DO-NOT-UNIFY register remains binding.
Every response version remains monotonic per globally unique review_id across terminal and non-terminal siblings.
A generate_response job is considered in flight only for pending, dispatching, or dispatched status, while completed handling remains owned by each caller.
Tenant proof stays a whole top-level query because ci:tenant-scope strips subqueries and must see the account and active-business predicates.
PHI exception persistence and its notify_admin outbox enqueue remain atomic and deduplicated.
Route handlers remain composition roots and domain modules receive SQL executors explicitly.
Cache read and write failures remain fail-open; compute failures and BusinessNotFoundError remain uncached and propagate.
The shared reply-length limit remains 2000 characters on both client and server.
edge_cases: Invalid JSON bodies still produce the same fallbacks in both client state machines.
A completed outbox without a usable draft retains its surface-specific idle, importing, response lookup, or failure behavior.
A discarded or failed prior response still advances the next response version rather than reusing version 1.
An archived location or a review owned by another account still fails ownership proof.
A duplicate open PHI exception still suppresses repeat notification.
A pending import decision with a null deadline remains not-an-offer, and a reactivation run never counts as the completed initial import.
Cache hits return parsed payloads without compute work; cache read or write failures serve a fresh payload.

rollback_plan: Revert the issue-765 refactor as one change; no schema, persisted-data, external-contract, flag, or dependency rollback is required. The existing route, worker, consent, and cache implementations remain recoverable from the fixed merge base.
observability: Existing reportCaughtError and worker logger/Sentry events keep their current source tags and error classes.
